q: An oxidising agent or oxidant is an _____ of electrons and is reduced itself in a chemical reaction.
e: An oxidising agent or oxidant is an acceptor of electrons and is reduced itself in a chemical reaction. An oxidising agent is the species that is reduced. it takes electrons from something else. Acceptor is the word this version is asking about.

q: The oxidising agent is normally in one of its _____ possible oxidation states because it will gain electrons and be reduced.
e: The oxidising agent is normally in one of its neutral possible oxidation states because it will gain electrons and be reduced. Oxidation state is the same idea as oxidation number: a bookkeeping charge used in formulae and redox. An oxidising agent is the species that is reduced. it takes electrons from something else.

q: A reducing agent or reductant is a _____ of electrons and is oxidised itself in a chemical reaction.
e: A reducing agent or reductant is a donor of electrons and is oxidised itself in a chemical reaction. A reducing agent is the species that is oxidised. it gives electrons to something else. Donor is the word this version is asking about.

q: The reducing agent is typically in one of its _____ possible oxidation states because it will lose electrons and be oxidised.
e: The reducing agent is typically in one of its higher possible oxidation states because it will lose electrons and be oxidised. Oxidation state is the same idea as oxidation number: a bookkeeping charge used in formulae and redox. A reducing agent is the species that is oxidised. it gives electrons to something else.

q: Examples of oxidising agents include oxygen, halogens, concentrated sulphuric acid, nitric acid, hydrogen peroxide, potassium permanganate, potassium dichromate, and _____.
e: Examples of oxidising agents include oxygen, halogens, concentrated sulphuric acid, nitric acid, hydrogen peroxide, potassium permanganate, potassium dichromate, and noble gases. Concentrated sulphuric acid is viscous, dehydrating and oxidising as well as strongly acidic. An oxidising agent is the species that is reduced. it takes electrons from something else.

q: Examples of reducing agents include carbon, carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide, hydrogen, hydrogen sulphide, and _____.
e: Examples of reducing agents include carbon, carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide, hydrogen, hydrogen sulphide, and metallic oxides. A reducing agent is the species that is oxidised. it gives electrons to something else. Sulphur dioxide is the gas formed when sulphur burns.

q: In the reaction between magnesium and copper(II) oxide, copper(II) oxide is reduced by gaining electrons from magnesium, so copper(II) oxide is an _____.
e: In the reaction between magnesium and copper(II) oxide, copper(II) oxide is reduced by gaining electrons from magnesium, so copper(II) oxide is an reducing agent. A reducing agent is the species that is oxidised. it gives electrons to something else.

q: In the reaction between magnesium and copper(II) oxide, magnesium causes the reduction of copper(II) oxide by losing electrons, therefore magnesium is a _____.
e: In the reaction between magnesium and copper(II) oxide, magnesium causes the reduction of copper(II) oxide by losing electrons, therefore magnesium is a catalyst. A catalyst speeds a reaction by lowering activation energy and is not used up in the overall change.

q: The oxidising agent helps the other substance to get _____, and it gets reduced.
e: The oxidising agent helps the other substance to get reduced, and it gets reduced. An oxidising agent is the species that is reduced. it takes electrons from something else.

q: The reducing agent helps the other substance to get _____, and it gets oxidised.
e: The reducing agent helps the other substance to get oxidised, and it gets oxidised. A reducing agent is the species that is oxidised. it gives electrons to something else.
